title: Magnetic Force Between Two Balls
statement:
There are `n` baskets on a number line. The `i`-th basket sits at the integer position `position[i]`; all positions are distinct and are given in no particular order.

You have `m` balls and must put each ball into a **different** basket. The magnetic force between two balls placed at positions `x` and `y` is `|x - y|`.

Choose the baskets so that the **minimum** force between any two of the `m` balls is as large as possible, and report that maximum possible minimum force. (This is the same task as placing `m` servers, cows or other items into given slots so that the closest pair is as far apart as possible.)

Because `m ≥ 2`, the minimum force is always defined.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `m`.
The second line contains `n` integers `position[0] ... position[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the largest possible value of the minimum distance between two chosen baskets.

examples.explanation: Put balls at positions 1, 4 and 8: the gaps are 3 and 4, so the minimum force is 3. A minimum of 4 is impossible: after 1 the next ball must be at 5 or more, i.e. at 8, and then no basket is at least 4 beyond 8.
With only two balls, put them in the two most distant baskets, 3 and 100, for a force of 97.

complexity.time: O(n log n + n log(max position))
complexity.space: O(1) extra beyond the sorted array

hints: Sort the positions. The answer is between 1 and `(max - min) / (m - 1)`.
Ask a yes/no question: can `m` balls be placed so that every two are at least `d` apart? This is monotone in `d` (if `d` works, any smaller distance works).
Check a given `d` greedily: put the first ball in the leftmost basket, then always put the next ball in the first basket at least `d` away from the previous ball. Binary search on `d`.
